assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration in electron lenses is a clear, well-defined invention that broke a barrier recognised since Scherzer's 1936 theorem. It brought routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atoms, interfaces and defects, and underpins a large share of modern materials physics, nanoscience and catalysis. I work in this field, so I weigh it with first-hand knowledge of how much it changed practice, and I acknowledge that familiarity as a possible bias.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical design of the multipole corrector, Haider led the implementation of the hexapole corrector in a working microscope, and Urban led the TEM correction experiments and the demonstration on materials. This is a natural three-person configuration. From memory, Ondrej Krivanek's role in the STEM corrector is a real competing claim that this candidate's credited names do not allow me to propose, and I have not verified the details.
assessment.maturity: Demonstrations date from the late 1990s and the instruments have been commercial and ubiquitous for well over a decade, with independent confirmation worldwide. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Krivanek's STEM aberration-corrector contribution is not among the credited names, so the allocation of credit across TEM and STEM correction is unresolved.
Some may see this as enabling instrumentation rather than a discovery, though 'invention' is an explicit criterion.
I have not independently verified the precise dates and priorities.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles, followed by experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, opened moire quantum matter. The idea is original, conceptually clear and has spawned a broad field including twisted TMDs and fractional Chern insulators.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discoveries. Theory plus experiment gives a clean three-person split. The credit of the experimental collaborators and co-authors, and of earlier work on twisted graphene, is a possible dispute I cannot resolve.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent groups reproduced the phases within a few years and the field is large and active. Some questions on the origin of superconductivity remain open, but the original discovery is robust and timely.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states remain debated.
Other experimental groups and earlier theoretical work on twisted layers could challenge the credit allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, using the magic-wavelength idea, is a distinct invention that gives the best frequency standards at the 10^-18 level and is moving toward a redefinition of the second. It also opens routes to tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first realised it with strontium; Ye's group developed and pushed the lattice clock to record accuracy. Two laureates is a fair configuration. Hall and Hansch (2005) already recognised combs, so Ye's clock role is distinct.
assessment.maturity: The idea has been realised and confirmed by several independent laboratories with several species, and the SI second redefinition roadmap is in progress. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Whether prize-level credit should also include other early contributors (for example Takamoto, or ion-clock pioneers) is unclear from the supplied names.
The relation to the earlier 2012 prize for ion control could be seen as overlapping.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, with experimental confirmation in HgTe wells, started a major field of topological materials. It is conceptually deep, original and widely consequential, although it builds on the 2016 topological-phase recognition.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction, and Molenkamp's group made the experimental discovery in HgTe wells (with Zhang and Bernevig's prediction there, who are not credited here). The three credited names give a plausible theory plus experiment split, but the omission of Bernevig and Zhang is a credit concern I cannot settle.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many materials and by ARPES and transport on 3D topological insulators; the field is stable and mature.
uncertainties: The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe prediction is not among the credited names, so the allocation is unresolved.
Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phases may count against novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realise clean, tunable Hubbard models, such as the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, and have become the workhorse of quantum simulation. The impact on many-body physics is significant, though the discovery is a collective programme more than a single result.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and coworkers) supplied the theoretical proposal, and Greiner and Bloch carried out and developed the experiments. Esslinger (fermions, Fermi-Hubbard) is also deserving, and a three-person cap forces a difficult choice. The first Mott insulator experiment involved Hansch's group as well, which may complicate priorities.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed worldwide, with the field now at the stage of quantum gas microscopes. Mature, with overlap in time with the ultracold atom and quantum information prizes.
uncertainties: Choosing three from four credited names (Esslinger excluded) is difficult.
It is a compound programme, so the specific discovery to honour is not unique.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond gave a room-temperature solid-state qubit and nanoscale sensor for magnetic fields, temperature and spins, with applications from materials to biology. Original and with lasting impact, and relevant to my own interest in nanoscale imaging and sensing.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's 1997 single-centre detection and Jelezko's coherent control are the key early contributions. Lukin and others developed sensing and nanoscale NMR; Awschalom and others also contributed, and a fair allocation remains contested.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many groups, with commercial instruments. The sensing applications are still maturing, so some parts could be premature.
uncertainties: Whether the prize centres on single-spin detection or on sensing applications is unclear.
Lukin's credit for sensing and the role of other groups cannot be resolved from the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: SASE X-ray free-electron lasers give femtosecond coherent X-ray pulses and have made time-resolved structural science possible. Impact on imaging and spectroscopy of matter is large, and I judge them favourably as a user of such tools, though the prize needs a distinct physics discovery.
assessment.attribution: The SASE concept came from Kondratenko and Saldin, and Bonifacio, Pellegrini and Narducci, with Kim contributing theory and design; the first lasing at LCLS and FLASH involved large teams. Allocation across theory, accelerator realisation and facility builders is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Several facilities (FLASH, LCLS, SACLA, European XFEL) confirm the principle; science output is rich.
uncertainties: Credit is distributed among many accelerator physicists and facility teams.
Parts of the SASE history (Kondratenko, Bonifacio, Murphy, Madey) fall outside the credited names, so allocation is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the later association with the blazar TXS 0506+056, opened neutrino astronomy and established a new messenger. A genuine discovery with large instrumentation.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube; Karle and Spiering held key leadership roles in the collaboration. A collaboration of hundreds makes the choice of three people contestable, and the credited names are only a subset of the plausible leaders.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is well established, but the source identification is still developing, so the full picture is not yet stable.
uncertainties: The astrophysical sources are largely unidentified.
Allocation among IceCube leaders and AMANDA founders is unresolved.
